title: Semi-Supervised Graph Imbalanced Regression

problem.claim: Graph regression tasks can suffer from imbalanced continuous label distributions, with rare label values under-represented in training data.

gap.claim: Annotated graph datasets for molecule and polymer property prediction are often small because labeling is expensive, limiting examples of rare label values.

contributions.claim: A semi-supervised framework progressively balances training data and reduces model bias through self-training.
The framework pseudo-labels graphs for under-represented labels using a regression confidence measurement and augments remaining rare-label examples in latent space.
The framework uses a label-anchored mixup algorithm to target balanced training data after pseudo-labeling.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe the regression confidence measurement and label-anchored mixup algorithm as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report experiments on seven regression tasks using graph datasets.
The authors report that the framework significantly reduces predicted graph-property error, especially in under-represented label areas.

narrative_sequence.summary: Regression data can be imbalanced, and rare continuous label values are difficult to collect.
Molecule and polymer graph datasets are often small because annotation requires expensive equipment and effort.
The proposed semi-supervised framework uses self-training to progressively balance data and reduce model bias.
It selects confidently pseudo-labeled examples using a reverse sampling distribution and applies label-anchored latent-space mixup to remaining rare labels.
Experiments cover seven graph regression tasks, with reported error reductions concentrated in under-represented label areas.

source_observation.claim: The framework combines pseudo-label selection with reverse-distribution sampling for under-represented labels.

interpretation.claim: Using confidence and targeted sampling can direct unlabeled-data expansion toward distributional deficiencies.

application.claim: For imbalanced regression, prioritize unlabeled examples that address rare-label regions rather than expanding the dataset uniformly.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the confidence calibration, sampling risks, or conditions under which pseudo-labeling fails.

source_observation.claim: Latent-space augmentation with label-anchored mixup is used after pseudo-label balancing to address remaining rare labels.

interpretation.claim: Sequentially combining data selection and targeted augmentation may help approach a desired label distribution.

application.claim: When pseudo-labeling does not fully resolve rare-label scarcity, apply targeted latent-space augmentation to the remaining gaps.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether latent-space interpolation preserves valid graph properties across all tasks.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify dataset names, task details, baselines, or quantitative error values.
The abstract does not describe the confidence measurement, self-training schedule, or mixup implementation in detail.
